In contrast, \( E_D(w) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{l \in D} (y^{(l)} - o^{(l)})^2 \) denotes the total error over a set of training examples \( D \), summing up the individual errors \( E_l(w) \) for each example in the dataset. This distinction highlights the incremental nature of the error calculation in the former, focusing on one example at a time, versus the aggregated error across multiple examples in the latter, which is more commonly used in batch mode training.
